title: Dual Goal Representations
claim: Instead of representing a state by its raw features, represent it by its relations to every other state.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, central 'Dualize' arrow, dashed edges to central node
description: Two rounded square panels sit side by side, linked by a horizontal arrow labeled 'Dualize'. The left panel, titled 'Original Representation', shows five gray state nodes (s1 to s5) scattered on a faint dashed grid. A goal node g, highlighted in blue, sits near the center. The formula φ^original(g) = g appears at the bottom. The right panel, titled 'Dual Representation' with 'Dual' in blue, has the same node layout. Blue dashed lines now connect g to each of the five states s1 to s5, like a star graph. Its formula reads φ^∨(g) = [d*(s1,g), ..., d*(s5,g)]^⊤. The eye goes first to the blue goal node and the blue dashed edges. The style is monochrome gray with blue as the only accent.
caption: Dual goal representations. A dual goal representation $\phi^\vee(g)$ is defined as the set of temporal distances $d^*(\cdot, g)$ from all other states. This representation has a number of appealing properties: it only depends on the intrinsic dynamics of the environment, contains sufficient information to express an optimal goal-reaching policy, and is able to discard exogenous noise.
abstract: In this work, we introduce dual goal representations for goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (GCRL). A dual goal representation characterizes a state by "the set of temporal distances from all other states"; in other words, it encodes a state through its relations to every other state, measured by temporal distance. This representation provides several appealing theoretical properties. First, it depends only on the intrinsic dynamics of the environment and is invariant to the original state representation. Second, it contains provably sufficient information to recover an optimal goal-reaching policy, while being able to filter out exogenous noise. Based on this concept, we develop a practical goal representation learning method that can be combined with any existing GCRL algorithm. Through diverse experiments on the OGBench task suite, we empirically show that dual goal representations consistently improve offline goal-reaching performance across 20 state- and pixel-based tasks.
